A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
wind turbines in north-western Europe have a short greenhouse gas payback period, which is mainly driven by the spatial and temporal variability of wind speed.
the payback times for wind turbines can be calculated using a simple formula, which is dependent on the wind resource, the wind turbine size and the time of installation.
the greenhouse gas paybacks times of wind turbines in NW-Europe are highly dependent on wind climate and turbine size.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the greenhouse gas paybacks of wind turbines are highly dependent on location-specific wind conditions.
the environmental benefits of wind energy depend strongly on the wind climate, which is a location-specific feature.
wind turbines’ greenhouse gas benefits depend on the local wind speed distribution and turbine size, which are location-dependent.
